the prostate is the only organ that has both androgen and oestro‐gen receptors and that the ratio of androgen to oestrogen is critical in determining the balance between pro‐liferation and apoptosis.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of steroid aromatase and steroid 5α-reductase (5AR) in prostate cancer and late-onset hypogonadal (LOH) male infertility.
the development of the theory of prostate carcinogenesis.
the role of steroid hormones in the pathophysiology of late‐onset androgen deficiency (LOAD), prostate cancer, and benign prostatic hypertrophy (BPH).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

prostate cancer is the result of a combination of a genetic defect in the androgen‐receptor gene and an environmental factor (i.e. low steroid 5AR) that results in an increase in oestrogen and a decrease in androgen.
low 5AR results not only in prostate cancer but also in late‐onset androgen deficiency (LOAD).
low 5α‐Reductase (5α‐R) activity results in a high oestrogen/testosterone ratio, which is the cause of late onset hypogonadotrophic hypogonadisim (LOH).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pitts unified model is a comprehensive model for the pathophysiology of prostate cancer and late‐onset male hypogonadotropic hypogonadim (LOHH) [21–24].

5α‐Reductase‐2 deficiency in males and aromatase deficiency in males and females results in the same clinical phenotype: late‐onset male hypogonadotropic hypogonadis, late‐on set prostate cancer and late‐onset osteoporosis.
5α‐Reductase is the key enzyme for the development of late‐onset androgen deficiency and prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pitts Unified Theory of Prostate Cancer and Hypogonadism, which has been published in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2013, and 2014, is validated by our current work.
the 5α‐redcutase inhibitors, finasteride and dutasteride, have the potential to prevent or delay the progression of low‐risk prostate cancer to high‐risk cancer.
the Pitts Unified Theory of Prostate Cancer, Late‐Onset Hypogonadism, and Carcinoma is validated by the data.
